what_its_for: Pirtobrutinib is a cancer medicine used to treat certain types of blood cancers. It is approved for adults with mantle cell lymphoma (MCL) who have already tried at least two other treatments, including a type of medicine called a BTK inhibitor. It may also be used for chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL) or small lymphocytic lymphoma (SLL) in certain patients who have already received specific prior treatments. Your doctor has prescribed this medicine because it helps slow or stop the growth of cancer cells.
how_to_take: Take pirtobrutinib by mouth (swallow the tablet whole) once a day, with or without food. Do not crush, break, or chew the tablet. Try to take it at the same time every day. If you vomit after taking your dose, do not take another dose that day — just take your next dose at the regular time tomorrow.
dosing: The usual adult dose is 200 mg (two 100 mg tablets) taken by mouth once daily. Your doctor may lower your dose if you have side effects. Always take the exact dose your doctor prescribes. Do not change your dose on your own.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember on the same day. If it is already the next day, skip the missed dose and take your next regular dose at the usual time. Never take two doses in one day to make up for a missed dose.
storage: Store pirtobrutinib tablets at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C and 25°C). Keep the tablets in their original container. Keep this medicine away from moisture, heat, and direct light. Keep it out of reach of children and pets. Do not flush unused medicine down the toilet — ask your pharmacist about the best way to dispose of leftover medicine.
what_to_avoid: Avoid grapefruit, grapefruit juice, Seville oranges, and starfruit while taking this medicine, as they can increase the amount of drug in your blood and raise the risk of side effects. Tell your doctor and pharmacist about ALL other medicines you take, including over-the-counter drugs, vitamins, and herbal supplements. Some medicines can interact with pirtobrutinib — especially blood thinners, antifungals, antibiotics, seizure medicines, and St. John's Wort. Avoid activities that could increase your risk of bleeding (such as contact sports) because this medicine may affect your blood's ability to clot. Do not receive live vaccines while on this treatment without first talking to your doctor.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you experience: unusual bleeding or bruising, blood in your urine or stool, coughing or vomiting blood, fast or irregular heartbeat or palpitations, shortness of breath or chest pain, signs of infection such as fever, chills, or body aches, severe diarrhea or stomach pain, vision changes, confusion or difficulty speaking, weakness or numbness on one side of the body (possible stroke signs), or any new or worsening symptoms that concern you. Also tell your doctor if you develop skin rash, swollen lymph nodes, or extreme fatigue.
when_it_works: You may not feel different right away. Cancer medicines often work quietly in the background. Some patients begin to see improvement in their symptoms or test results within the first few weeks to months of treatment. Your doctor will monitor you with regular blood tests and check-ups to see how the medicine is working. Keep taking it as prescribed even if you feel well, unless your doctor tells you to stop.
special_populations: Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Pirtobrutinib can harm an unborn baby. If you can become pregnant, use effective birth control during treatment and for at least 1 week after your last dose. If you are a male with a female partner who can become pregnant, use contraception during treatment and for 1 week after the last dose. Do not breastfeed while taking this medicine and for 1 week after your last dose. Kidney or liver problems: Your doctor may adjust your dose if you have moderate to severe liver problems. Tell your doctor about any kidney or liver conditions. Older adults: Older patients can take this medicine, but may need to be watched more closely for side effects. Pediatric use: This medicine is not currently approved for use in children.
